news
New hot spell forecast next week in France – highs of 30C but no heatwave
Lack of rain will deepen drought crisis
Weather in the south of France, including in Aix-en-Provence (pictured) may feel more summery than autumnal over the next two weeks
Uvamen/Shutterstock
France is set for a new bout of warm weather next week, with temperatures again climbing above 30C across the south for several days.
A high-pressure anticyclone system will move in from the Atlantic, covering the country with calm and sunny skies.
Concentrated in the south, the effects of the system will slowly extend northwards as the week progresses, where despite occasional clouds it should remain dry and warm.
Early forecasts for this weekend predict a calm weekend with temperatures above average, reaching 24C in the north and 28C in the south on Sunday (September 13).
Starting in earnest Monday (September 14), the anticyclone will initially weaken in the middle of the week before getting progressively stronger, reaching to cover all of France by the end (September 17 - 18).
Remarkably, it may stay above France for an entire week until it moves eastwards on September 24 - 25, bringing calm and warm conditions to the country for several days.
While France is seeing a drop in temperatures alongside several bouts of rain this week, September has otherwise been marked with intense warm weather and a late heatwave.
This included a new overall September high of 40.3C in Tarn.
Another heatwave?
The conditions will coincide with an increase in temperatures, both from the anticyclone winds themselves and the lack of disturbances (no colder polar winds, storms, etc).
Temperatures of 30C and above are forecast across the south at several points during the anticyclone spell, and in the north highs of 20C will be the temporary norm, potentially reaching above 25C on some days.
These are well above seasonal norms for the season, particularly in the latter half of the month. This, coupled with the calm and sunny conditions, will give a warmer-than-usual feel to the month.
However, it is not expected that heatwave conditions will be raised, as departmental temperatures are unlikely to break required three-day thresholds.
Overnight temperatures will remain chilly despite the warm days, and for departmental warnings to be issued overnight temperatures are typically required to be above certain levels for three days – levels not set to be reached during the spell.
Temperatures will equally not be warm enough to reach national heatwave levels (overall daily temperatures of 23.4C, with at least one day over 25.3C), due to the cooler evening and night-time temperatures.
Further impact on drought
The calm and dry conditions may be positive news for some, but the lack of rain only spells bad news for France’s deepening drought crisis.
Current models predict hardly any rain – if any at all – to fall until the beginning of the following week (September 21), and even then this is set to be light drizzle.
France desperately needs consistent rain this autumn to replenish historically low aquifers and reservoirs, but for these to be replenished soils must first be wet enough to allow rainfall to permeate.
Several months of drought conditions and successive heatwaves have dried out soils, and a prolonged dryspell in September will only make it harder for soils to become permeable.
At the same time, intense downpours associated with storms also fail to replenish reservoirs, as rain falls too quickly and harshly to be permeated, and instead stays above ground level often causing floods.
Early predictions of an intense El Niño weather event this winter mean that days could be warmer and sunnier, but storms wetter and more violent – neither condition conducive to ending drought conditions.
It means that water usage restrictions may apply throughout the winter, depending on aquifer levels.

articles.title: Indy heats up - The Butler Collegian

articles.full_text:
A week-long heat wave hit Indianapolis at the start of September, sending temperatures into the high 90s and hitting feels-like temperatures over 100 degrees. While this heat wave was four degrees off from record temperatures, it has been over 10 degrees warmer than the yearly averages.
Extreme heat can be deadly for people who are experiencing homelessness and those without proper access to cooling. Vulnerable groups like children, the elderly and those with pre-existing medical conditions have a heightened risk for heat-related illness.
Junior computer science major DJ Dorchack expressed distaste for the continued heat, saying that even his car wouldn’t drive right because it was so hot.
“It [has been] so hot out, especially for September,” Dorchack said. “The whole week it was best to stay inside.”
Professor Thomas Paradis began college as a meteorology major, and although he switched disciplines, he has always been interested in the weather. This led him to teach the Weather, Climate and Society Natural World course at the university — which has no traditional meteorology classes.
“It is relatively common to have a heat wave in September — the northern hemisphere is still heated up,” Paradis said. “We hit 96 degrees, but the record [is] 100 in 1953. This is [still] a significant heat wave because the average maximum temperature for this time of year is around 83. So the fact that it was 96 [on Sept. 1] means we were 13 degrees above normal.”
The sustained above-average heat occurred due to a phenomenon that is often referred to as a heat dome. This happens in the summer when high pressure pushes sinking air, making thunderstorms and rain unable to form. The sky is more likely to be cloudless under high pressure, letting the sun warm the Earth’s surface faster without intervention from storm clouds.
NWS senior meteorologist Mike Ryan provided insight into the weather patterns that led to the heat wave.
“In August, the [heat] was focused out to our west — [around] the Central Rockies,” Ryan said. “We were on the edge of that ridge of high pressure, so storms were moving around it, and the ridge is over us now. That’s why, if you look at the radar right now, all the storms have been up north of the Great Lakes because, again, we’re under that area of high pressure now, and it’s very, very hot.”
Ryan explained that the heat should once again shift west, but not until after over a week of hot, humid weather. He also emphasized the significance of the heatwave, with 2026 being the first year since 2012 with three days straight of over 95 degrees in early September.
As part of the NWS’s responsibilities, they work to inform central Indiana of the weather and potential advisories, like the heat advisory that has been in effect. These advisories, graphics and information are shared on their various social media platforms, as well as the NWS website.
The NWS works closely with city and county officials, and they coordinate with the Red Cross and other health organizations.
“Health has become a much bigger topic with weather, especially when it comes to things like this [heat],” Ryan said. “[We say], this is what we’re anticipating, and they can take that information and apply it to utilize cooling centers and other things like that.”
For people like the construction workers on campus, staying hydrated and taking breaks in air conditioning can help prevent heat-related illness. Those in Indianapolis who do not have access to air conditioning, cool water or are experiencing homelessness need to rely on assistance from health organizations like the Red Cross. However, in the wake of recent disastrous flooding, resources may be more limited.

articles.full_text:
Baaritaan lagu ogaaday in cabidda waxyaaba aadka u kulul ay kordhin karto khatarta kansarka
Article Information
Author, Michelle Roberts
Role, Digital health editor
Published
Waqtiga akhriska: 3 daqiiqo
Cilmi-baaris laga sameeyay UK ayaa soo jeedinaysa in si joogto ah loo cabo cabitaanno sida shaaha iyo kafeega oo aad u kulul ay kordhin karto khatarta kansarka ku dhaca dhuunta ama, oo loo yaqaan kansarka hunguriga.
Cilmi-baarayaashu waxay sheegeen in natiijooyinkan, oo laga helay daraasad lagu sameeyay ku dhowaad hal milyan oo qof, ay yihiin kuwa ugu ballaaran ilaa hadda ee caddeynaya xiriirka ka dhexeeya cabbitaannada aadka u kulul iyo kansarkan.
Daraasadda ayaa muujisay in dadka cabbitaannadooda ku tilmaamay "aad u kulul" ay qiyaastii saddex jeer ku badan tahay khatarta kansarkan marka loo eego dadka cabba shaah ama qaxwo "diirran". Si kastaba ha ahaatee, khubaradu waxay carrabka ku adkeeyeen in fursadda guud ee qofku ugu dhaco kansarkan ay weli hooseyso.
Cabitaannada aadka u kulul ee dhuunta ka gudbaya una sii socda caloosha wuxuu dhaawici karaa xuubka unugyada gudaha ee dhuunta cuntada.
Shaaha ama kafeega kulul
Shaqadan cilmi-baarista ah oo ay samaysay Jaamacadda Oxford, laguna daabacay International Journal of Cancer, ayaa cabitaan kasta oo heerkulkiisu yahay 65°C ama ka badan ku qeexaysa inuu yahay mid "aad u kulul" oo keeni kara khatar caafimaad.
Sida laga soo xigtay xog laga ururiyey 977,282 rag iyo dumar ah oo da'doodu dhexdhexaad tahay, cabbidda lix ama in ka badan oo cabitaanno kulul ah maalintii ayaa sidoo kale kordhinaysa khatarta.
Inkasta oo caanaha lagu daro ay cabitaanka wax yar qaboojin karaan, haddana shaah ama qaxwo caano leh ayaa weli laga yaabaa inuu aad u kulul yahay, ayay cilmi-baarayaashu sheegeen.
Hay'adda Cancer Research UK waxay sheegtay inay adag tahay in waqti sax ah loo cayimo inta ay tahay in cabitaan kulul la sugo si uu u qaboobo.
Warbixinada qotada dheer iyo wararka BBC Somali oo toos kuugu imanaaya WhatsApp.
Halkaan kaga soo biir
Dhamaadka xayeysiinta
"Balse haddii aad ka welwelsan tahay, waxaan kugula talin lahayn inaad sugto ilaa cabitaanku noqdo mid si raaxo leh loo cabbi karo, halkii aad cabbi lahayd isagoo weli aad u kulul," ayay hay'addu tiri.
Cilmi-baaraha hoggaaminaysay daraasadda, Dr Keren Papier, ayaa sheegtay in cilmi-baaris hore oo Koonfurta Ameerika laga sameeyay—halkaas oo dad badan ay cabbaan cabitaan geedo laga sameeyo oo aad u kulul oo loo yaqaan mate, ay horey u muujisay xiriir la mid ah oo u dhexeeya cabitaannada kulul iyo kansarka hunguriga.
Laakiin waxay tiri: "Hadda waxaa loo baahan yahay cilmi-baaris dheeraad ah si loo ogaado heerkulka saxda ah ee cabitaannada ee lala xiriirin karo khatartan korodhay."
Daraasad kale oo lagu sameeyay 118 qof oo da'yar, kuwaas oo dhowr jeer dhadhamiyay noocyo kala duwan oo qaxwo madow ah, ayaa lagu ogaaday in dadka badankoodu cabitaanka u arkeen inuu aad u kulul yahay marka heerkulku gaaro 70°C ama ka badan.
Sida laga soo xigtay shirkad samaysa koobabka qaxwaha la qaato, heerkulka ugu habboon ee qaxwaha kulul ee la cabayo waa inta u dhaxaysa 49°C iyo 60°C.
Halista guud
Cilmi-baarayaashu waxay qiyaasayaan in qiyaastii hal ama laba ka mid ah 10-kii kiis ee kansarka hunguriga laga hortagi karo haddii dadku joojiyaan cabbidda cabitaannada aadka u kulul.
Kansarka hunguriga ee loo yaqaan squamous cell oesophageal cancer waa nooc dhif ah, waxaana sannad kasta uu ku dhacaa dhowr kun oo qof. Dalka UK, qiyaastii 1% dadka ayaa halis ugu jira inay noloshooda mar uun ku dhacaan noocan kansarka ah.
Sidaas darteed, xitaa haddii cabitaannada aadka u kulul ay kordhin karaan khatarta qofka, haddana fursadda uu qofku ku qaadi karo kansarkan weli waa hooseysaa.
Waxaa sidoo kale jira arrimo kale oo halis ah, sida sigaar-cabista, kuwaas oo khatar weyn u ah kansarka hunguriga.
Fiona Osgun oo ka tirsan Cancer Research UK, oo maalgelisay daraasaddan, ayaa carrabka ku adkaysay: "Hababka ugu muhiimsan ee lagu yareyn karo khatarta kansarkan waa in aan la cabin sigaarka iyo in la yareeyo cabbidda khamriga."
Calaamadaha kansarka hunguriga waxaa ka mid noqon kara laab-jeex, dheefshiid xumo, xanuun ku dhaca cunaha ama laabta, iyo miisaanka oo yaraada.

Hyderabad, Sept. 9: Telangana may receive rain in parts of the state over the next five days, according to the Meteorological Department.
The department has also issued a Yellow Alert for four districts. It has advised residents to remain alert as weather conditions may change in different areas.
Rain may occur along with thunderstorms and gusty winds in several parts of Telangana. Therefore, people in the alerted districts should take precautions during periods of severe weather.
The department expects cloudy skies to continue across the state. Meanwhile, some areas may receive light showers during the coming days.

Telangana rain forecast for northern districts
North Telangana may see light rainfall during the forecast period. In particular, Adilabad and Jagtial could receive slight showers.
The forecast indicates that rainfall will not remain uniform across the state. Instead, some areas may experience showers while other regions could mainly see cloudy conditions.
Thunderstorms and gusty winds could accompany rain in some places. Therefore, residents should remain cautious when weather conditions worsen.
The Yellow Alert in four districts signals the possibility of adverse weather. People in those districts should follow weather updates and local advisories.
Here To Join Us On WhatsApp
Telangana rain may bring thunderstorms
The expected weather pattern includes cloud cover, light showers and thunderstorms. Gusty winds may also affect some areas during the next five days.
However, the department has indicated chances of light rainfall in parts of North Telangana. Adilabad and Jagtial remain among the districts mentioned in the forecast.
Meanwhile, cloudy weather is likely to continue across Telangana. The changing conditions could bring brief showers in some locations.
The Meteorological Department has urged people to stay vigilant. Residents should also exercise caution during thunderstorms and strong winds.
Overall, Telangana may see a mix of cloudy skies and light rainfall over the next five days. The Yellow Alert also highlights the need for caution in the four affected districts.

articles.full_text:
MANILA, Philippines — Consumers may experience rotational brownouts anew across the Visayas grid on Wednesday, as more coal plants in the region and in Mindanao remain offline.
In an advisory, the National Grid Corp. of the Philippines said the Visayas would be under a red alert from 1 p.m. to 10 p.m.
Mindanao, which also provides additional supply to the Visayas, would face a yellow alert from 1 p.m. to 9 p.m. due to outages at two coal plants.
A yellow alert indicates that available power reserves are thinning, meaning any unexpected plant outage could trigger service interruptions. A red alert indicates that the supply cannot meet the demand, raising the risk of rotational brownouts unless we manage consumption effectively. /pai

articles.full_text:
Weather Headlines:
- Uncomfortable heat and humidity through Thursday.
- Showers and thunderstorms each afternoon and evening through Thursday, best chance near the mountains.
- High surf, strong rip currents and possible coastal flooding through Wednesday.
- Extreme Heat Warning for the coast and valleys until 8pm Wednesday, then a Heat Advisory will go into effect until 8pm Thursday.
- Extreme Heat Warning in the deserts Wednesday through Friday.
Wednesday will be just as hot and humid as it has been with dangerous beach conditions for another day and showers and thunderstorms over parts of the county.
Tuesday was another record-hot day with Poway soaring to 105 degrees! We'll be close to several records on Wednesday, including in Kearny Mesa, Escondido, Poway, Vista, Chula Vista and San Diego.
This hot and sticky weather will continue through Thursday with the worst of the heat and humidity through Wednesday.
An Extreme Heat Warning is in effect for the coast and valleys until 8pm Wednesday. The coast will experience temperatures between 85 and 97 degrees, and just 5 to 10 miles inland we'll start to see 100s. The inland areas will mostly be near 100 degrees.
When that ends at 8pm, a Heat Advisory will go into effect because it will still be hot, just not as hot as it's been. The Heat Advisory for the coast and valleys will continue through 8pm Thursday. You can expect mid-80s to low-90s at the coast and 90 to 102 inland.
A Heat Advisory is in effect for the mountain communities until 8pm Thursday for 90s bleow 5,500 feet.
An Extreme Heat Warning will be in effect for the deserts Wednesday through Friday for highs up to 112 degrees.
On top of the hot and humid days, the nights won't provide much relief, with warm and muggy nights. Temperatures will only drop to the mid-70s to low-80s for most coast and inland areas by sunrise, low-70s in the mountains and 80s in the deserts. That means you can expect 80s and 90s most of the evening and night for much of the county.
Most rainfall has been light, with heavier rain in thunderstorms. Isoalted to scattered storms are expected again Wednesday and Thursday in the afternoon and evening. Any storms may produce heavy rain, localized flooding, small hail and strong winds.
Click here to see real-time rainfall totals.
The Coastal Flood Advisory has been extended until 11pm Wednesday due to high surf and astronomical high tides leading to the threat of coastal flooding and beach erosion. High tide on Wednesday will be 6.3' at 8:38pm
There is relief in sight, though! Cooler and drier, less humid air is expected this weekend! Temperatures will drop back into the 70s along the coast, 80s inland, 70s and low-80s in the mountains, but still in the 100s in the deserts, but it will be a dry heat!
Fall is right around the corner with the Autumnal Equinox happening at 5:05pm on September 22nd.

Coast: 85-97°
Inland: 97-106°
Mountains: 83-99°
Deserts: 108-110°
